events.title: Anime Expo 2026
events.description: North America's largest anime convention, with four days of studio panels, world-premiere screenings, and an exhibit hall that swallows the entire convention centre. This year's headline draws were the MAPPA and Ufotable panels and a stacked artist alley in the South Hall.

events.title: Anime NYC 2026
events.description: The East Coast's flagship anime weekend, heavy on English dub premieres, industry licensing announcements, and late-night screening blocks. The River Pavilion stage runs cosplay competitions all three days.

events.title: Jump Festa 2027
events.description: Shueisha's annual two-day showcase and the single most important date on the anime announcement calendar. Studio adaptation reveals, stage events with voice cast, and the Super Stage panels are almost always where the next season's biggest series get confirmed.

events.title: Gamescom 2026
events.description: The world's largest games event by attendance, split between the consumer halls and the trade-only business area. Opening Night Live carried the marquee reveals, and the retro and indie halls were the busiest they have been in years.

events.title: Tokyo Game Show 2026
events.description: Japan's biggest games show, running two business days before the public halls open for the weekend. Expect the deepest hands-on floor of the year for Japanese publishers and a livestream schedule that runs around the clock.

events.title: The Game Awards 2026
events.description: The industry's year-end awards show, now just as much a reveal stream as a ceremony, with world premieres slotted between categories. Game of the Year is the headline, but the announcement reel is what most viewers tune in for.

events.title: San Diego Comic-Con International 2026
events.description: The original and still the biggest stage for film and television marketing, with Hall H panels that regularly make or break a release's early buzz. This year's Saturday slot was dominated by the 2027 superhero slate.

events.title: New York Comic Con 2026
events.description: ReedPop's East Coast counterpart to San Diego, with a stronger emphasis on publishing and a Main Stage that has become a regular home for autumn release trailers. The Empire Stage panels are the ones to queue early for.

events.title: Across the Spider-Verse IMAX Fan Screening Night
events.description: A one-night community re-release of the Spider-Verse films in IMAX ahead of the next chapter's marketing push, with a recorded introduction from the animation team. Several venues are running a costume-friendly screening alongside the standard showtimes.

events.title: ATX Television Festival 2026
events.description: A festival built specifically around television, with reunions, writers' room panels, and pilot screenings rather than red-carpet marketing. It is the one event where showrunners talk candidly about renewal decisions and cancellations.

events.title: Stranger Things Day Watch Party
events.description: The annual fan-created celebration of the date the series begins, marked with coordinated rewatches, 1980s-themed screenings, and a shared online watch-along. Community groups in most major cities run their own events under the same banner.

events.title: PaleyFest LA 2027
events.description: The Paley Center's flagship television festival, where full casts appear on stage for panel discussions and preview footage. It reliably lands the season's most-watched drama and comedy ensembles.

events.title: KCON LA 2026
events.description: The largest K-pop convention outside Korea, combining an artist lineup of evening concerts with daytime panels, dance workshops, and a merchandise hall that queues around the block. The convention stage showcases are where most attendees discover their next favourite group.

events.title: MAMA Awards 2026
events.description: Mnet's annual Asian music awards, staged across three nights with a different themed lineup each evening. The performance stages are treated as full productions rather than award-show filler, which is why the show trends worldwide every year.

events.title: Random Dance Play in the Park
events.description: A free open-air meetup where choreography from the year's biggest comebacks is played at random and anyone who knows the routine steps in. It runs for three hours with a beginner-friendly circle at the edge of the square.

events.title: C2E2 2026
events.description: The Chicago Comic & Entertainment Expo, smaller than the coastal giants and better for it, with short lines to the artist alley and publisher panels that actually take questions. It has become the dependable spring stop for indie and small-press creators.

events.title: Thought Bubble Comic Art Festival 2026
events.description: A creator-first comics festival in North Yorkshire, built around the artist alley rather than celebrity signings, with a week of workshops and talks leading into the weekend halls. It is the best place in the UK to meet small-press and self-published cartoonists.

events.title: Free Comic Book Day 2027
events.description: The annual first-Saturday-of-May giveaway, when publishers print special issues and shops hand them out free to anyone who walks in. Many stores pair it with signings, cosplay, and a sale, and it is consistently the single busiest day of the year for local comic retail.

events.title: Comic Market 106 (Summer Comiket)
events.description: The world's largest self-published comics fair, where hundreds of thousands of attendees buy doujinshi directly from the creators who made them. The corporate hall carries publisher booths and exclusive merchandise, but the circles are the reason people queue before sunrise.

events.title: Manga Barcelona 2026
events.description: One of Europe's largest manga events, with a focus on Spanish-language publishing, author signings, and a cosplay championship that draws competitors from across the continent. The Japanese guest roster is usually announced in October.

events.title: Angoulême International Comics Festival 2027
events.description: The most prestigious comics festival in the world, treating the medium as literature across four days of exhibitions and awards. It spreads through the whole city rather than a convention hall, and the manga pavilion has grown substantially each year.
